label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
**One star for now: We need a working system and someone accountable**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Our migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, we have only been able to process checkouts offline on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped out—approximately 640 holds lost. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still do not have a resolution or a clear timetable.

Those failures have consequences beyond an inconvenient workday. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and sent him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been recording checkouts on index cards. With a staff our size, there is very little spare time to reconstruct records while keeping the doors open.

During sales, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we received was a shared inbox. That gap between the promise and the support delivered is central to this review.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demonstration, and the staff interface is better than our previous system. I still see value in the product’s design. But a better interface does not make up for interrupted circulation, missing holds, and support that gives us no useful next step.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and the library’s line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain what we are paying for and when reliable service will be restored.

I am asking a senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week, identify who owns our case, and provide a concrete recovery plan, including whether the lost holds can be recovered.

To other small-library directors: get support response times, escalation procedures, and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing.

One star for now. I will revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves these problems and follows through.
